- Primary deployment preference: Dedicated capacity (isolation + predictable throughput).
- Use cases: real-time chat (low-latency) + batch report generation (longer context).
- Initial TPS target: 40-60 requests/sec during peak, with sporadic bursts to ~100 rps.
- Concurrency: expected 8-16 simultaneous active sessions producing tokens at once.
- Token mix (est): 75% short interactions (~150 tokens total), 25% long generations (~1,200 tokens total).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 500ms for short/chat calls; p99 < 2s preferred.

Attachments: I'm sending a sizing workbook (redwood_dedicated_sizing_v1.xlsx) with the call breakdown and a draft SOW.

Next steps:
1) Aditya: can you validate GPU recommendation and rough GPU count based on the token mix + model family we discussed (Llama-2-70B equivalent/quantized)?
2) Sam: confirm whether encryption at rest + customer-managed KMS required (we noted they likely are).
3) I'll follow up with a draft procurement timeline and preliminary pricing for Dedicated.

Thanks — appreciate the details.

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up — initial sizing (H100 vs A100)

Hi all —

I ran an initial sizing pass based on their inputs (model: Llama-2-70B class, quantized FP16/INT8-like profile). High level notes below; I've updated the workbook with the math (see redwood_dedicated_sizing_v1.xlsx).

Assumptions used:
- Short request: 150 tokens avg (includes prompt + response).
- Long request: 1,200 tokens avg.
- Token generation cost is dominated by decoder pass; inputs are small relative to generation.
- Batch window: 20-50ms for low latency requests (bounded by p95 SLO).

Throughput estimates (tokens/sec per GPU, approx):
- H100 (optimized kernels, NVLink, large memory): ~55k-70k tokens/sec per GPU for this model profile (varies with quant profile).
- A100 (80GB): ~30k-40k tokens/sec per GPU.

Translate to requests/sec given token mix (75% short, 25% long):
- Effective avg tokens/request = 0.75*150 + 0.25*1200 = 412.5 tokens/request.
- H100: 55k tokens/sec / 412.5 ≈ 133 req/sec per GPU (conservative lower bound ~120 req/s to honor latency).
- A100: 30k tokens/sec / 412.5 ≈ 72 req/sec per GPU (conservative ~60 req/s).

Sizing guidance for Brightline target (50 rps sustained, 100 rps burst):
- H100 option: 1 GPU provides ~120 req/s sustained (conservative). To handle 100 rps bursts + headroom and HA, propose 2 GPUs active + 1 hot spare for rolling updates (total 3 GPUs).
- A100 option: 2 GPUs active (≈ 120 req/s aggregate conservative) + 1 spare => total 3 GPUs. Note A100 will have higher latency headroom constraints and less room for additional growth.

Cost-per-1M tokens (very rough, includes infra + amortized GPU cost):
- H100: estimated $X.XX per 1M tokens (please treat as placeholder until procurement pricing confirmed).
- A100: estimated $Y.YY per 1M tokens (lower up-front instance cost but lower throughput, so cost per token can be comparable).

Operational notes:
- Use autoscale policy based on queue length + p95 latency; allow burst capacity to spin up extra GPUs if burst > sustained by >30s.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys in Private/Dedicated; will require an integration window in the onboarding plan.

I'll add a slide in the workbook showing the p95/p99 latency sensitivity vs batch window; we should review with them on the follow-up call.

—Aditya
